en: The Buddha spoke the *Sūtra on the Past Buddhas’ Almsround*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Yuezhi during the Western Jin Dynasty. The Buddha said:
"In a past age, there was a Buddha who entered a city for alms, accompanied by his honored disciples and various bodhisattvas..."

"Sākyamuni; the disciples and bodhisattvas, with their physical forms and marks of excellence, are all perfectly upright and handsome. According to their original practices, each has attained their respective path.
There was a woman who had been pregnant for several months; seeing the Buddha and the Sangha proceeding on their journey, she made this aspiration within her heart:
"The child I carry shall, upon birth, become a śramaṇa and a disciple of the Buddha.

When the months were fulfilled, he was born in safety; the boy was also exceptionally beautiful, different from others. Although his mother, out of affection, had no intention of letting the boy go forth as a śramaṇa, the boy conceived an awareness within himself and thought to himself:
"I previously made a vow that if I were to have a son, I would cause him to enter the Way."

"The child is now born, yet he is unlike ordinary men—he brings me peace and security—and there is no foul discharge. It would be contrary to my original resolve to harbor lingering attachment to the bonds of affection."

"When my son was seven years old, our family was again poor and lived in cramped quarters; so I prepared food for two people and three dharma robes, took a water flask in my hand, and went with my son to the place where the Buddha was."
He prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I pray that you will have compassion for my son and allow him to become a śramaṇa, so that he may later attain the Way and his physical form shall be like yours.
The Buddha immediately granted his request and ordained him as a śramaṇa.
The mother took a rinsing pitcher and washed the child’s hands; immediately, nine dragons emerged from the mouth of the vessel and poured water into the child’s hands.
When the washing was finished, the remaining water scattered over the child’s head, and the trickling drops upon his head transformed into a jeweled canopy with interlaced nets of pearls.

Within it was a lion throne, upon which sat a Buddha. The Buddha smiled, and from his mouth issued light of five colors that illuminated ten billion buddha-fields; the light then returned, circled the Buddha’s body, and entered through the crown of the boy’s head.

The mother presented the food and utensils before the Buddha and ate her son’s portion as well; she then gave rise to the aspiration for supreme, impartial enlightenment. At that moment, ten billion buddha-fields shook in six ways, and the Buddhas of all those fields appeared spontaneously.
The Buddha ate his mother’s food until he was full, and all those Buddhas and the assembly of bhikṣus were likewise fully satisfied; yet the food remained as it was, without being diminished.
The mother was immediately filled with joy, and countless devas and humans all attained the stage of avaivartika.
At that time, the boy’s hair fell off and he became a śramaṇa, immediately attaining the stage of non-retrogression.
His mother then addressed the Buddha:
"What I have now seen contains three wonders: [text continues]"
That nine dragons spouted water to wash my son’s hands was the first marvel;
that after he had washed, the remaining water scattered over his head and transformed into a jeweled canopy, and that there was a Buddha seated upon a lion throne, was the second marvel;
and that the Buddha smiled and light from his mouth entered through the crown of my son’s head was the third marvel.
“I pray that the Buddha will explain this to me in detail!

The Buddha said, “This child shall become a Buddha fourteen kalpas hence. That nine dragons shall bathe him, the lion throne, the flower canopy, the jeweled pavilion, and the light from the Buddha’s smile entering through the child’s crown—all these are his destined responses.”

Upon hearing the Buddha’s words, the mother felt redoubled joy; she thought that after seven hundred lifetimes as a mother of a Cakravartin King had passed and the lifespan of that kalpa was exhausted, she would transition from her female body and attain the stage of *avaivartika*.
The Buddha said,
"That child at that time was my own self.
Such are the merits I now possess in this world."
The devas, nāgas, spirits, and all the people, having heard what the Buddha taught, all attained the stage of *avaivartika*.
The Sūtra on the Past Buddhas’ Alms-Round, spoken by the Buddhas: Aśoka Buddha, Svabhāva-śūnyatā Buddha, Devarāja Buddha, Suvarṇaprabha Buddha.
